A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MICRO study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations on reasoning and behavioral benchmarks, expert ablations, routing analyses, and neuroscience-localizer experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds annotation-agreement analysis, MMLU-Pro evaluations, inference-routing experiments, and hybrid 8B model results.

M1.justification: The original architecture and three-stage curriculum remain unchanged. Appendix M adds a hybrid Llama-3.1-8B variant with experts only in the final 12 layers and dense earlier layers, a limited architectural adaptation of MICRO.

E1.justification: v3 adds MMLU-Pro as a separate knowledge/reasoning evaluation set in Figure 7 and Tables 7–8. Existing training data, behavioral evaluations, medical benchmarks, and other reasoning datasets remain. The annotation analysis revisits existing MICRO_SFT data, while the scaling experiments reuse retained tasks.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Dense, MoB, and ablated MoB controls, with MoE comparisons also retained in the appendix. The new 8B study instantiates these existing comparator classes at a different model configuration; it introduces no new competing approach.

E3.justification: v3 adds protocols for MMLU-Pro evaluation (five-shot CoT; 12,032 test items), three-annotator label validation, top-1 versus top-2 inference, and hybrid 8B models. The majority-label comparison uses 240 items, excluding 13 ties. Figure 7 averages now cover five benchmarks instead of four. Existing main training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New appendices directly test pseudo-label reliability, sensitivity to the number of active inference experts, and specialization in the hybrid 8B model through routing, ablations, and localizers. Figure 21 reports failed localizer recovery in that hybrid configuration. These substantially extend validation beyond v2's retained ablations, training-stability, DPO, and medical-domain analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix B adds chance-corrected agreement statistics, including Krippendorff's alpha and Fleiss' and Cohen's kappa. Appendix M adds paired Wilcoxon tests across nine benchmarks, reporting p=0.18 against Dense and p=0.10 against MoB. Existing CogBench five-seed reporting, standard errors, and Welch tests remain; no increase in repeated training runs is documented.

E6.justification: v3 adds agreement, MMLU-Pro, inference-scaling, and 8B results. Table 12 reports averages of 46.3% and 47.3% under top-1 and top-2 routing; Table 13 reports 54.2 for MICRO-8B versus 54.7 for Dense and 54.8 for MoB. Figure 5 revises several 3B localizer percentages. Figure 7 averages change with benchmark composition, while retained benchmark-table entries stay unchanged.

T1.justification: The dataset/routing definitions and bounded relative error similarity formula remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added statistical analyses introduce no new formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: brain-inspired specialization, causal interpretability, inference steering, and competitive reasoning performance and behavioral alignment. Additional experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2's brief scaling and expert-expansion limitations become a substantially broader discussion in v3, covering the 8B boundary, untested training-data size sensitivity, pseudo-label quality, SFT/DPO-only post-training, and CogBench-only behavioral validation. New analyses interpret moderate annotation agreement and qualify scaling through the hybrid model's unsuccessful localizer recovery and degradation beyond two active experts.

D1.justification: v3 adds a demo access link alongside the existing code/data/model link, identifies the mmlu_pro evaluation-harness task, and discloses that the new human annotations were produced exclusively by the authors. Existing main training hyperparameters and data-construction instructions remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted references, including Binhuraib et al. on Topoformer, Tuckute et al.'s neuroscience review, and Kean et al. on abstract formal reasoning. Default-mode discussion replaces Hassabis and Maguire with more targeted supporting citations. The claimed novelty relative to modular language models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text wording and the central section sequence are retained. Changes comprise localized background edits, expanded discussion and limitations, an ethics statement, inserted appendix sections, updated cross-references, and the conference-publication header, rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: New agreement and scaling tables and hybrid-8B routing/localizer figures substantially expand the evidence displays. Figure 7 gains MMLU-Pro panels, the benchmark tables gain corresponding columns, and Figure 5 gains color scales. Most existing appendix plots and steering examples are retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical substantiation and transparency through direct pseudo-label validation, inference-scaling tests, larger-model evaluation, and more specific limitations. The gains are qualified: annotation agreement is moderate, and the 8B experiment uses a hybrid architecture whose localizers fail to recover the intended experts (Figure 21). These additions clarify the evidence and its boundaries without substantially resolving full-architecture scaling or changing the paper's central support.
